_comment: Adapter pins declared to produce identical scores for a suite, so that rows
recorded under one may be reused when another is running.
An adapter pin is sha256 over the suite adapter and _common.py together, and
most of _common.py is the generation path: streaming, retries, admission. A
change there moves the pin without changing how an existing row was scored.
The reuse check cannot tell those apart, so it refuses by default and reads
this file for the cases somebody has actually established.
A group is a set of pins whose scores are identical FOR THAT SUITE. Membership
is a claim about evidence, not a convenience: state what was compared. Nothing
belongs here because rescoring it would be expensive.

bfcl_v4.why: Both versions run the same scoring code on any row that did not time out. score_response is byte-identical between them, and run_item differs only by an `if response is None:` branch that the newer version drops -- that branch is reachable only when request_with_retries exhausts its retries. Verified structurally rather than by reading: parsing both, removing that one If node from the older run_item, and comparing the ASTs gives equality. The remaining textual differences are the fallback import path and a docstring path, both from the 2026-08-17 move of scripts/ under eval/. Rows carrying a timeout are independently refused by suite_is_current, so the dropped branch cannot have run on anything this group admits; every arm on disk records timeouts=0. Recorded pin is commit 0054003, running pin is HEAD.

livecodebench_v6.why: livecodebench.py is git blob 7811a91915 in all three, so the code that extracts and executes the program is the same file. The only _common.py change reaching score_response is unpack_choice reading reasoning through reasoning_field, which additionally accepts a 'reasoning' key; the stored responses carry 'reasoning_content' only, so split_reasoning receives the same string and the extracted block is the same. Verified by diffing 6706f52..87a0a86..148e667.
